topic: Dossier: tự host app tìm việc để AI viết CV và thư xin việc riêng cho từng tin tuyển dụng

repos.name: dossier
repos.description: A self-hosted job search app that writes tailored resumes and cover letters from your profile.

notes.audience: Lập trình viên và người tự host VPS muốn quản lý dữ liệu tìm việc trên máy chủ riêng, dùng AI viết CV và cover letter chuẩn theo từng JD mà không sợ bịa kinh nghiệm hay lộ thông tin cá nhân.
notes.angle: Đang tìm việc mà vẫn muốn giữ hồ sơ và CV trên máy chủ của mình thì đây là cách AI viết CV riêng cho từng tin tuyển dụng, không bịa kinh nghiệm.

facts.fact: Dossier lưu trữ toàn bộ lịch sử sự nghiệp trong một hồ sơ gốc duy nhất và tự động tạo CV cùng thư xin việc riêng biệt cho từng tin tuyển dụng.
facts.quote: Dossier keeps your career history in one profile and turns it into a clean resume. For every job you apply to, it reads the posting, shows how you match, and drafts a tailored resume and cover letter

facts.fact: AI của Dossier chỉ dùng thông tin có sẵn trong hồ sơ của bạn; những yêu cầu trong JD mà bạn chưa có sẽ được đánh dấu là khoảng trống chứ tuyệt đối không bịa đặt kinh nghiệm.
facts.quote: Never invents experience: drafts only use facts from your profile. What the posting asks for and your profile doesn't have is shown as a gap, not made up.

facts.fact: Hệ thống hỗ trợ cả AI local chạy qua Ollama / LM Studio (giữ dữ liệu 100% trên phần cứng riêng) lẫn các mô hình hosted như OpenAI API, Anthropic hoặc Mistral.
facts.quote: That can be a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, so your profile and documents stay on your own hardware, or a hosted one (any OpenAI-compatible API, Anthropic or Mistral)

facts.fact: Dossier được thiết kế chuyên biệt cho một người dùng trên máy chủ nhỏ, chỉ cần một mật khẩu quản trị và lưu trữ vào PostgreSQL hoặc một file SQLite duy nhất.
facts.quote: It's for one person on a small server: one password, your data in your own PostgreSQL database (or a single SQLite file), and an AI model of your choice.

facts.fact: Cấu hình khuyến nghị cho VPS để tự host Dossier mượt mà là tối thiểu 2 vCPU và 2 GB RAM.
facts.quote: Give the server at least 2 vCPUs and 2 GB of memory (see Performance and sizing).

facts.fact: Container Dossier tiêu tốn tối đa khoảng 520 MB RAM (đã bao gồm Chromium để xuất file), do đó container cần được cấp ít nhất 768 MB RAM.
facts.quote: Dossier used at most about 520 MB, Chromium included, so give the container at least 768 MB.

facts.fact: Kích thước Docker image tải về lần đầu vào khoảng 1.7 GB.
facts.quote: The first start downloads the image (about 1.7 GB) and sets up the database.

facts.fact: Hỗ trợ 12 theme CV tạo sẵn cùng công cụ dựng theme trực tiếp và xuất bản PDF trực tiếp trên server.
facts.quote: Base resume: twelve themes and a theme builder, previewed live and printed to PDF on the server. Duplicate themes, or share them as files.

facts.fact: Tích hợp sẵn tính năng tìm việc qua JSearch (quét LinkedIn, Indeed), Adzuna hoặc FreeHire (trang tuyển dụng của công ty).
facts.quote: search postings near your city, or anywhere you choose, through JSearch (LinkedIn, Indeed and more), Adzuna or FreeHire

facts.fact: Tự động thu thập và chấm điểm bài đăng tuyển dụng từ danh sách YC startups và bài thảo luận hàng tháng 'Who is hiring?' trên Hacker News theo địa điểm hoặc remote.
facts.quote: startups that are hiring, from YC startups' job posts and Hacker News' monthly “Who is hiring?” thread, kept to the ones that hire where you live or remotely from your country

facts.fact: Job Agent tự động chạy tìm kiếm mỗi ngày một lần, chấm điểm tin tuyển dụng theo hồ sơ của bạn và soạn sẵn bản nháp để bạn duyệt.
facts.quote: once a day it runs one search for you, skips what you've seen, scores the new postings against your profile and keeps the best on the Agent screen, with its reasons.

facts.fact: Job Agent không bao giờ tự động nộp đơn hay gửi email thay bạn, mọi hành động gửi đi đều phải do người dùng quyết định.
facts.quote: It can prepare tailored drafts too, which wait for your review. It never sends or applies.

facts.fact: Mật khẩu đăng nhập được mã hóa an toàn bằng Argon2id và hệ thống chỉ lưu chuỗi băm, không bao giờ lưu mật khẩu gốc.
facts.quote: Add that line to .env as DOSSIER_PASSWORD=argon2id:…, with any text editor. Dossier only keeps the hash, never the password.

facts.fact: Có thể chạy chế độ rút gọn không cần PostgreSQL bằng cách dùng SQLite lưu vào volume /data.
facts.quote: Put DATABASE_URL=file:/data/dossier.db in .env and run the image on its own, with a volume for /data:

facts.fact: Hỗ trợ kết nối giao thức MCP (Model Context Protocol) để điều khiển tìm việc và soạn CV trực tiếp từ ứng dụng Claude hoặc n8n.
facts.quote: MCP connector (optional): use Dossier from Claude, on claude.ai, in the Desktop and mobile apps or in Claude's command-line app, on your own Claude plan, or from another MCP app such as n8n.

facts.fact: Có tùy chọn kết nối Gmail và Google Calendar để đọc thư phản hồi của nhà tuyển dụng, gợi ý câu trả lời và đồng bộ lịch phỏng vấn hai chiều.
facts.quote: Gmail and Calendar (optional): connect your Google account to send an application from your own address with its PDFs attached, see employers' replies next to each application

facts.fact: Mã nguồn mở miễn phí theo giấy phép GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0).
facts.quote: Dossier is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0.

caveats: Chỉ hỗ trợ giao diện trên máy tính (Desktop/Laptop), không tối ưu cho trình duyệt điện thoại.
Hệ thống chỉ dành cho một người dùng duy nhất với 1 hồ sơ và 1 mật khẩu, không có tính năng phân quyền nhiều tài khoản.
Giao diện phần mềm chỉ hỗ trợ tiếng Anh (mặc dù tài liệu xuất ra hỗ trợ 21 ngôn ngữ tích hợp sẵn).
Mỗi cơ sở dữ liệu chỉ được chạy duy nhất một instance Dossier vì hàng đợi tác vụ AI, tác vụ sao lưu ban đêm và trình duyệt xuất PDF chạy bên trong tiến trình của app.
Docker image được build cho kiến trúc amd64, nên nếu chạy trên Mac Apple Silicon cần khai báo cấu hình giả lập linux/amd64.
gaps: Dossier có hỗ trợ tiếng Việt là một trong 21 ngôn ngữ xuất văn bản (tiêu đề, ngày tháng) chuẩn hay phải dùng chế độ 'Other language' (giữ tiêu đề tiếng Anh)?
Khi tự host mô hình AI qua Ollama trên cùng VPS, mô hình cụ thể nào (như Qwen 2.5 hay Llama 3.1) cho kết quả trích xuất và viết CV bằng tiếng Việt tốt nhất mà vẫn nhẹ RAM?
Các API tìm việc như JSearch, Adzuna có cần trả phí hoặc giới hạn số lượt request miễn phí mỗi tháng hay không?

## reactive-resume/reactive-resume (https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume)
Description: A one-of-a-kind resume builder that keeps your privacy in mind. Completely secure, customizable, portable, open-source and free forever. Try it out today!
Homepage: https://rxresu.me
Language: TypeScript; license: MIT; created 2020-03-25; last push 2026-11-04
Latest release: v6.0.9 (2026-10-29)
README (start):
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Reactive Resume now lives at **[`reactive-resume/reactive-resume`](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume)** on GitHub.  
> GHCR images publish to `ghcr.io/reactive-resume/reactive-resume`.  
> Docker Hub stays at `amruthpillai/reactive-resume`.

  
    
  

  Reactive Resume

  Reactive Resume is a free and open-source resume builder for writing resumes and cover letters, checking your work, and tracking job applications.

  
    Get Started
    ·
    Learn More
  

  
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
  

  Sponsored by

  
    
      
        
          
            
            
          
        
      
      
        
          
            
            
          
        
      
      
        
          
            
            
          
        
      
      
        
          
        
      
    
  

---

Create a free account, import an existing resume or start fresh, and see the finished page as you write. Download a PDF, Word, Markdown, or JSON file, or share your resume with a public link. You can also run the whole application on your own infrastructure.

You own your data. The codebase is open source under the MIT license, with no tracking, no ads, and no paid tier. Optional AI features use a provider you connect; hosting and provider usage may have their own costs.

## Build a better resume, together

[Join the Reactive Resume community on Discord](https://discord.gg/u9pAd3za9t) to exchange resume feedback, get help using or self-hosting the app, and share ideas with other users and contributors.

- **Resume feedback:** post a redacted resume and one specific question, or help someone improve theirs.
- **Help:** find troubleshooting discussions and ask questions in dedicated forum threads.
- **Contribute:** discuss ideas, translations, and code with the people building Reactive Resume.

Feedback comes from fellow community members. Remove contact details and other private information before posting.

## Features

**Write, Design, and Check**

- Redesigned editor with inline content editing and click-to-select on the page
- Live PDF preview and browser downloads powered by Forme, rendered in a background worker
- Rich text, custom sections, drag-and-drop ordering, and structured dates with consistent formatting
- Autosave, local recovery of unsaved resume drafts, and up to 200 undo steps
- Phone and tablet layouts, keyboard shortcuts, and a searchable command bar

**Templates and Customization**

- 18 templates, including the new Porygon and Smeargle, previewed with your own content
- One-column, two-column, and ATS-safe template filters
- Font presets, custom fonts, colors, spacing, A4 and Letter paper, and left or right sidebars
- Fit overflowing content by adjusting density, margins, and text size
- Custom Styles written as Semantic CSS, with an element picker on the page

**Resume Checks**

- Readability checks with findings pinned to the relevant lines
- Job-posting keyword matching and a view of the text hiring software reads
- Checks on the exported PDF, plus an optional AI writing review
- A public [ATS checker](https://rxresu.me/ats-checker) that reads PDFs in your browser without an account

**Documents and Cover Letters**

- One searchable library for resumes and letters, with tags, sorting, and grid or list views
- Standalone cover letters with their own editor, exports, and version history
- Link a letter to a resume to keep its sender details and design in sync, or customize it independently
- Automatic and named versions you can preview and restore
- Trash with Undo and a 30-day recovery window

**Job Applications**

- List, Board, Insights, and Calendar views for tracking applications from Saved to Offer
- Save jobs from a URL or pasted posting; optional keyword search through Firecrawl, Tavily, or Exa
- Tailor a resume and draft a cover letter for a saved job
- Track contacts, notes, follow-ups, application outcomes, and the documents you sent
- Schedule interviews, export calendar events, and import or export applications as CSV

**AI Assistant**

- Assistant beside your resume or letter, with conversations tied to that document
- Proposed edits show what changes and why; accept or reject each suggestion
- Improve selected text, review writing, and draft letters from a resume and job posting
- Connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, or other supported providers and compatible endpoints
- Optional web search and page reading; self-hosters can configure shared AI and web-access providers

**Import, Export, and Sharing**

- Import Reactive Resume JSON, JSON Resume, LinkedIn data exports, PDF, and Word files
- JSON, LinkedIn, and readable PDF imports work without AI; Word imports require a connected provider
- Export resumes and letters as PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown, or JSON
- Share resumes through public links with optional password protection and view/download statistics
- REST API and MCP server for document management, imports, exports, checks, and application workflows

**Privacy and Control**

- Self-host with Docker, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, or a 1-click deploy on Hostinger
- No tracking or ads; export your account data or delete your account
- Passkeys, two-factor authentication, and linked sign-in providers
- Multiple interface languages, light/dark/system themes, and reduced-motion support

## Quick Start

Use the [hosted app](https://rxresu.me) to start writing, or build this checkout locally with Docker and Docker Compose:

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume.git reactive-resume
cd reactive-resume

# Create your local configuration
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env: set AUTH_SECRET and a separate ENCRYPTION_SECRET.
# Generate each secret with: openssl rand -hex 32

# Build the app and start PostgreSQL, Redis, and SeaweedFS
docker compose up -d --build

# Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser
```

This builds the checked-out source. For a deployment using published images, follow the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker). For source development, see the [development setup guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development).

## Tech Stack

| Category         | Technology                               |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Web app          | React 19 SPA, TanStack Router, and Vite  |
| Server           | Hono on Node.js 24 or Cloudflare Workers |
| Language         | TypeScript                               |
| Monorepo         | pnpm and Turborepo                       |
| Database         | PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM              |
| API              | oRPC, OpenAPI REST, and MCP              |
| Auth             | Better Auth                              |
| Styling          | Tailwind CSS                             |
| UI Components    | Base UI + shared UI package              |
| State Management | Zustand + TanStack Query                 |
| PDF rendering    | Forme, with PDF.js for the viewer        |
| Rich text        | TipTap                                   |
| Localization     | Lingui                                   |

## Self-Hosting

Reactive Resume runs the same application everywhere: PostgreSQL for data, plus storage for uploads. Pick the option that fits how much you want to manage.

| Option                                          | Best for                                      | Guide                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Hostinger](#hostinger)                         | A ready-made VPS with no setup                | [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger)                                                    |
| [Vercel](#vercel)                               | Serverless, with managed database and storage | [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel)                                                          |

## career-ops-hq/career-ops (https://github.com/career-ops-hq/career-ops)
Description: Open-source AI job search agent and job finder: scan job boards, score each job 1-5 against your CV before you apply, tailor an ATS-friendly resume and cover letter, get interview prep and an application tracker. It helps you fill in each application; you press Submit. Runs locally in Codex, OpenCode and other AI CLIs, or as a Claude Code plugin.
Homepage: https://career-ops.org
Language: JavaScript; license: MIT; created 2026-04-04; last push 2026-11-05
Latest release: career-ops-v1.38.0 (2026-10-23)
README (start):
The open-source AI job search agent.

  Created by @santifer, with    700+ contributors

Months of sending CVs into silence.
So I built the filter I needed.

740 listings evaluated. 68 applied. 12 interviews. 1 offer.
I was its first user. I got the job. Then I open-⁠sourced it.

Paste a job. On your machine, it tells you if it's still open and if it fits.
It tailors your CV and drafts your answers. You press Submit.

  

My own search, partway through, with the UI in Spanish.

  Companies use AI to filter candidates.
  I just gave candidates AI to choose companies.

  Six months later, I left that job.
  Now we build career-ops, so you can land yours.

Try it on one job ↓ · Read the full story →
Prefer not to use a terminal? Join the waitlist for a web version →

The people who came after me wrote down how they got hired.

  

Every card is a public issue you can open. Landed yours? Leave your card →

⭐ If career-ops helped you, a star helps the next person find it.

  
      
  

  

  
      
  

## Your turn

Paste one job you were about to apply to tonight. If it comes back do not apply, you just got the night back. If it comes back with a plan, you know what to do next.

```bash
npx @santifer/career-ops init
```

Open source. Local. In the AI CLI you already use. Free and local models included.

## You don't have to search alone

The silence after you hit send is not about you. Enough people saw the same thing to write the practice down, in six lines:

> Apply better to fewer. Signal over volume. Evidence over keywords. A human decides. Local-first. Dignity on both sides of the table.

A few of them, in their own words.

  

Every signature is a commit you can audit. Read them all, or add yours → · What is AI job search?

Hiring will not fix itself. The people going through it can, and they are already in the room, comparing notes and fixing each other's setups.

[This is where the fix gets written](CONTRIBUTING.md). A room, not a club. **Let's build together.**

## Sponsors

career-ops is free for candidates, forever. These companies sponsor the project:

  

SerpApi · Build a portfolio project with live search data. SerpApi gives developers structured JSON/Markdown from Google Search, Maps, Shopping, and other engines through a simple API call.

> Sponsorship buys clearly labeled visibility, never influence: no amount of money changes the roadmap or places anything in the product. Sponsors never appear in evaluations, rankings or recommendations.

## What career-ops does for you

Paste a job. It tells you whether that night is worth it.

- **Still open?** It checks that the posting is still live before you write a word.
- **Not you?** It scores the role against your real CV and tells you to skip a weak fit. You can override it.
- **Worth it?** It drafts the CV, the cover letter and the answers. You read them. You send them.
- **Who do I talk to?** It finds the person and drafts the note. It never sends it.
- **Where does it all go?** Every application stays on your machine. Nothing is uploaded to us.
- **What should I learn?** After a run of noes, it names the gap.

The first runs are rough. It does not know you yet. Talk to it: your CV, what you want, what you refuse. Think of it as a recruiter's first week.

On first launch it asks for all that in chat. Nothing to configure by hand.

## What career-ops will not do

- **Auto-submit an application.** It drafts the answer to every field; you review and click Submit. The script never POSTs (`prepare-application.mjs`).
- **Send an email.** Drafts only. There is no mail transport anywhere in this codebase.
- **Phone home.** No telemetry, no backend of ours. Your CV goes from your machine to the AI provider you chose, and nowhere else. The only public ledger is this repo: `HIRED.md` and its issues.
- **Push you to apply below 4.0/5.** It will tell you not to. You can override it, and it will say so.

It reformulates your CV; it must never fabricate it. A check in code stops a PDF whose numbers or facts appear in neither your CV nor your article digest, but it cannot judge every rewording yet. Read every CV before you send it. Details in the [FAQ](#faq).

## Features

| Feature                  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A-H Evaluation**       | Role summary, CV match (with how much each requirement matters for this posting, and whether that weight came from the JD's own wording, its structure, or an estimate, labelled per requirement; an estimate can never be top-band), level strategy, comp research, personalization, interview prep (STAR+R) -- plus a Block G posting-legitimacy check (is it still open, is it a repost: observations, not verdicts), and a Work-Auth signal that flags an explicit no-sponsorship JD as a hard blocker |
| **Human-in-the-Loop**    | AI evaluates and recommends, you decide and act. The system never submits an application -- you always have the final call                |
| **ATS PDF Generation**   | ATS-readable CVs tailored to each JD from your own experience, in Space Grotesk + DM Sans design                                                                                 |
| **Cover Letter Generator** | Research-backed cover letters with keyword mirroring, four interactive angle prompts (why/problems/approach/tone), draft-in-chat approval gate, and A4 PDF via the same HTML + Playwright pipeline as CVs. Auto-drafts on every evaluation; complete and generate on demand via `/career-ops cover` |
| **Beyond the CV**        | Company research ([`deep`](modes/deep.md)) surfaces AI strategy, recent moves, engineering culture, and the angle your profile should take. Contact discovery ([`contacto`](modes/contacto.md)) identifies the hiring manager, recruiter, or team peer worth reaching out to and drafts a ≤300-character LinkedIn message tuned to each contact type. Formal application email drafts ([`email`](modes/email.md)) turn an evaluated report or pasted JD into a subject line, body, and attachment checklist without sending, submitting, or clicking anything. Applications get you in the queue; research gets you a conversation. |
| **Pattern Analysis**     | Rejection patterns and per-ATS-channel advance rates (`analyze-patterns.mjs`), lifetime funnel stats (`stats.mjs`), repost detection, a possible sign of a ghost job (`detect-reposts.mjs`) |

Everything else it does

| Feature                  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Auto-Pipeline**        | Paste a URL, get a full evaluation + PDF + tracker entry                                                                                 |
| **Interview Story Bank** | Accumulates STAR+Reflection stories across evaluations -- 5-10 master stories you can adapt to the behavioral questions you get                        |
| **Negotiation Scripts**  | Salary negotiation frameworks, geographic discount pushback, competing offer leverage                                                    |
| **Application Email Drafts** | Formal recruiter/referral/cold application emails from a report or pasted JD, with subject line, attachment checklist, source-backed fit points, and a profile-driven contact block. Draft-only -- career-ops never sends, submits, or clicks anything. |
| **Portal Scanner**       | 100+ companies pre-configured (Anthropic, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Retool, n8n...) + custom web-search queries across Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever, Wellfound |
| **Funded Company Discovery** | Review-first `npm run company:funded` script surfaces recently funded companies and source diagnostics from structured public feeds without editing your data |
| **Batch Processing**     | Parallel evaluation with headless CLI workers (`claude -p` / `opencode run`)                                                             |
| **Dashboard TUI**        | Terminal UI to browse, filter, and sort your pipeline                                                                                    |
| **Pipeline Integrity**   | Automated merge, dedup, status normalization, health checks                                                                              |
| **Interview Suite**      | Time-blocked prep plans, practice sessions with feedback, post-interview debriefs ([`interview/`](modes/interview/README.md)), and a company red-flag detector ([`interview-redflag`](modes/interview-redflag.md)) |
| **Offer Stage**          | Contract reading companion -- clause walk plus a lawyer question list ([`offer-prep`](modes/offer-prep.md)) -- and a desired/advertised/actual salary-gap analyzer (`salary-gap.mjs`) |
| **Follow-ups & Replies** | Follow-up cadence calculator and seeded reminders (`followup-cadence.mjs`, `followup-seed.mjs`); turn them off with `follow_ups.enabled: false` in `config/profile.yml`; employer reply classification into tracker updates ([`reply-watch`](modes/reply-watch.md)) |
| **Plugin System**        | Opt-in integrations (Gmail, Notion, Apify + a community registry), disabled by default -- see [docs/PLUGINS.md](docs/PLUGINS.md)        |
| **LinkedIn job alerts**  | Paste a LinkedIn alert email on the dashboard or with `node linkedin-import.mjs`. No Google account. See [docs/LINKEDIN_JOBS.md](docs/LINKEDIN_JOBS.md) |

Dossier

Your job search, on your own server: one profile, a tailored resume and cover letter for every job, and every application tracked from draft to offer.

     

Dossier keeps your career history in one profile and turns it into a clean resume. For every job you apply to, it reads the posting, shows how you match, and drafts a tailored resume and cover letter that only use facts from your profile. You refine them in a chat, download them as PDFs and track each application from draft to offer.

It's for one person on a small server: one password, your data in your own PostgreSQL database (or a single SQLite file), and an AI model of your choice. That can be a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, so your profile and documents stay on your own hardware, or a hosted one (any OpenAI-compatible API, Anthropic or Mistral), which then receives what it writes from. Privacy says what goes where.

Get started: run it on your computer in a few minutes, or self-host it on a server. The installation guide covers every way: Docker with or without Compose, Node.js, a plain Ubuntu server, CapRover, Coolify and Dokploy.

Demo

Recorded with the demo data (Jane Doe is made up) and a stand-in AI server that answers at once, played at 1.2× speed. With a real model, reading a posting and writing the documents takes from a few seconds to a few minutes.

Features
Profile: basics, skills and languages, experience, projects, education, publications and references, in the order you choose, with a strength meter that counts only what a profile needs. Projects (side, open-source, course or thesis work) show what you can do where your job titles don't yet. Publications are cited in your own style, with bold and italics, and go on resumes word for word. Start it from an existing resume (PDF, Word or Markdown) if you like.
Base resume: twelve themes and a theme builder, previewed live and printed to PDF on the server. Duplicate themes, or share them as files.
Find jobs: search postings near your city, or anywhere you choose, through JSearch (LinkedIn, Indeed and more), Adzuna or FreeHire (company career pages). Save the good ones, dismiss the rest, score any of them against your profile, and start an application from a posting with one click.
Startups: startups that are hiring, from YC startups' job posts and Hacker News' monthly “Who is hiring?” thread, kept to the ones that hire where you live or remotely from your country and ranked against your profile, with the address each one publishes for applications. Dossier reads their sites politely and follows their robots.txt. Start an application to one with a click; you decide whom to write to.
Job agent (optional): once a day it runs one search for you, skips what you've seen, scores the new postings against your profile and keeps the best on the Agent screen, with its reasons. It can prepare tailored drafts too, which wait for your review. It never sends or applies.
New application: paste a posting; Dossier pulls out the details and requirements, matches them against your profile, and writes a tailored resume and cover letter in the tone you pick.
Never invents experience: drafts only use facts from your profile. What the posting asks for and your profile doesn't have is shown as a gap, not made up.
Refine: ask for changes in a chat, edit or regenerate any part (every part of the cover letter too: sender, date, recipient, greeting and sign-off, written in the letter's language), undo AI changes or go back to any earlier version, keep private notes.
Send: an email to go with each application, to whoever the posting says to send it to, ready to copy or open in your mail app, with the resume and cover letter PDFs to attach. Edit, rewrite or refine it like the documents.
MCP connector (optional): use Dossier from Claude, on claude.ai, in the Desktop and mobile apps or in Claude's command-line app, on your own Claude plan, or from another MCP app such as n8n. Claude can search for jobs, score them against your profile, read your profile and applications, and save the resume and cover letter it writes as a Draft, checked like Dossier's own. It never sends or deletes anything. Without an AI model of Dossier's own, Write it with Claude hands a posting to a new Claude chat. Turn it on in Settings → MCP connector (see Connecting Claude).
Gmail and Calendar (optional): connect your Google account to send an application from your own address with its PDFs attached, see employers' replies next to each application, have the AI read what they ask and draft your answer from your profile, offer interview times you're free, and see your month and the week ahead on the dashboard, with interviews kept in step with Google Calendar both ways. Nothing is sent without your confirmation. Set it up by entering your Google OAuth client in Settings → Google, or with DOSSIER_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and DOSSIER_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET (see Connecting Gmail and Calendar).
Track: a board and a table of every application, and a dashboard with your funnel (last 30 days, 90 days or all time), a week-by-week chart, what's worth a look next, upcoming interviews included, and a calendar.
Your data: export and import everything as one file, nightly backups, and Delete everything.

Run it on your computer

All you need is Docker Desktop on macOS or Windows, or Docker Engine with its Compose plugin on Linux, and about 2 GB of free memory. Run the commands in a terminal: macOS's Terminal, Linux, or WSL on Windows.

1. Fetch the Compose file into a folder of its own, and make the secrets Dossier needs:

mkdir ~/dossier && cd ~/dossier
curl -fsSL -o compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AienTech/dossier/main/compose.production.yml
echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)" > .env
echo "DOSSIER_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)" >> .env

On an Apple Silicon Mac, also run printf 'services:\n  app:\n    platform: linux/amd64\n' > compose.override.yml: the image is built for Intel and AMD processors, and Docker Desktop runs it under emulation.

2. Choose your password. This asks for it twice and prints a hash of it, one line that starts with argon2id::

docker run --rm -it --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/aientech/dossier hash-password

Add that line to .env as DOSSIER_PASSWORD=argon2id:…, with any text editor. Dossier only keeps the hash, never the password.

3. Start it:

docker compose up -d

The first start downloads the image (about 1.7 GB) and sets up the database. Open http://localhost:3000, sign in with your password, and pick an AI model in Settings → AI provider (see Choosing an AI provider).

docker compose stop stops it and docker compose start starts it again, with your data kept.

Without a database server: Dossier can keep its data in an SQLite file instead, in one container. Put DATABASE_URL=file:/data/dossier.db in .env and run the image on its own, with a volume for /data:

docker run -d --name dossier --env-file .env -v dossier-data:/data -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 ghcr.io/aientech/dossier

Without that volume, the next upgrade deletes the data, and the container warns about it when it starts. To back up the file, stop the container and copy dossier.db out of the volume. PostgreSQL stays the better choice on a shared server; to move between the two, export your data in Settings → Your data and import it on the other. It's only reachable from your own computer. The installation guide's Docker Compose page has more: another port, your time zone, upgrades and removing it.

Self-hosting

To put Dossier on a server, on your own domain with HTTPS, follow the installation guide: a plain Ubuntu server with Docker Compose and Caddy (or Node.js, without Docker), CapRover, Coolify or Dokploy. Give the server at least 2 vCPUs and 2 GB of memory (see Performance and sizing).

Documentation

The wiki has what comes after installing:

Choosing an AI provider: a hosted model, or a local one with Ollama or LM Studio.
Choosing a job source: JSearch, Adzuna or FreeHire (and an unofficial one for Germany), and the job agent.
Connecting Gmail and Calendar: your own Google OAuth client, step by step.
Connecting Claude: the MCP connector, in Claude's apps and on the command line.
Backups and restore: exports, nightly backups and database dumps.
Upgrading to a new version.
Troubleshooting: what the common errors mean, and what to do about them.
Privacy: what stays on your server and what leaves it. PRIVACY.md has the details.
Environment variables: every setting the server reads.
Known limitations
Desktop only: made for a laptop or desktop browser, not for phones.
Single user: one password and one profile; there are no accounts.
English interface: the app itself is in English. Documents can be written in other languages; in the 21 built-in ones, their headings, dates and language levels are in that language too, and in one added with Other language… those stay in English.
One instance: run a single copy of the app per database. The nightly backups, the AI job queue and the PDF browser live inside the app's process.
Performance and sizing

Measured on 28 September 2026 with the production build in a container limited to 2 vCPUs and 1 GB:

PDFs: the base resume renders in about 0.25 s, or 1 s when Chromium has to start first (it closes after five idle minutes). Two render at a time and the rest queue: six requested at once are done in 1.4 s. Dossier used at most about 520 MB, Chromium included, so give the container at least 768 MB.
Screens: with ten times the demo data (90 applications), the dashboard and the applications list answer in 20–90 ms, and every query takes under a millisecond. With 900 applications they take up to about 0.2 s, mostly rendering; the tables are indexed for the queries they get.
Interactions (changing a status, moving a card, switching tabs, opening an editor, typing, picking a theme) respond within 32 ms, and within about 100 ms on a CPU four times slower.

What protects your data, how to run Dossier safely and how to report a problem: see SECURITY.md.

Working on Dossier itself: see DEVELOPMENT.md.
